phase: Phase 2 — A2ASecBench Setup & First Controlled Security Benchmark

security_analysis.attack_mechanism: Agent Squatting (AS) constructs adversarial Agent Cards mimicking benign agent cards by copying semantic keywords, service descriptions, and skill declarations with subtle typographical, naming, or routing permutations.
security_analysis.sut_vulnerability: The keyword-overlap heuristic selector ranks candidates purely based on token overlap between the user prompt/task description and the agent's declared skills and descriptions. It lacks cryptographic identity verification, reputation scoring, provenance validation, and behavioral confirmation.
security_analysis.implication_for_a2a: In decentralized A2A multi-agent ecosystems, clients or orchestrators selecting sub-agents based solely on declared metadata in Agent Cards (agent-card.json) are acutely vulnerable to rogue agents intercepting sensitive workflows (89% ASR in this trial). Robust registry validation, cryptographic signatures, and behavioral trust models are required.
